queries: WITH ev AS (SELECT e.event_id, e.status, AVG(b.remaining) AS avg_rem, AVG((b.spent - b.amount) * 1.0 / b.amount) AS avg_over FROM budget b JOIN event e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event GROUP BY e.event_id, e.status), st AS (SELECT status, AVG(avg_rem) AS avg_remaining, AVG(avg_over) AS avg_overspend_rate FROM ev GROUP BY status) SELECT status, avg_remaining, avg_overspend_rate, avg_remaining / AVG(avg_remaining) OVER () AS remaining_relative_to_status_mean FROM st

responses.sql: WITH ev AS (SELECT e.event_id, e.status, AVG(b.remaining) AS avg_rem, AVG((b.spent - b.amount) * 1.0 / b.amount) AS avg_over FROM budget b JOIN event e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event GROUP BY e.event_id, e.status), st AS (SELECT status, AVG(avg_rem) AS avg_remaining, AVG(avg_over) AS avg_overspend_rate FROM ev GROUP BY status) SELECT status, avg_remaining, avg_overspend_rate, avg_remaining / AVG(avg_remaining) OVER () AS remaining_relative_to_status_mean FROM st

assumptions.assumption: Status means event.status (the matched event's status), not budget.event_status.
Budget lines with amount = 0 give a NULL overspend rate (division by zero yields NULL in SQLite) and are ignored in the average. Events whose lines are all NULL are ignored at the status level.
The mean of per-status averages is the unweighted mean over the status rows returned, and the last column is each status's average remaining divided by it.

alternatives.interpretation: Use the status recorded on the budget line (budget.event_status) to group events instead of event.status. Lines are still joined to events, and events are still averaged first.
alternatives.sql: WITH ev AS (SELECT e.event_id, b.event_status AS status, AVG(b.remaining) AS avg_rem, AVG((b.spent - b.amount) * 1.0 / b.amount) AS avg_over FROM budget b JOIN event e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event GROUP BY e.event_id, b.event_status), st AS (SELECT status, AVG(avg_rem) AS avg_remaining, AVG(avg_over) AS avg_overspend_rate FROM ev GROUP BY status) SELECT status, avg_remaining, avg_overspend_rate, avg_remaining / AVG(avg_remaining) OVER () AS remaining_relative_to_status_mean FROM st

assumptions.assumption: Status is event.status (the request says the event's status), not budget.event_status.
Budget lines with amount = 0 give an undefined overspend rate (NULLIF makes it NULL), so they are ignored in that average.
The 'simple mean of the per-status averages' is taken over the statuses returned, each weighted equally, using a window average over the per-status rows.

responses.sql: WITH ev AS (SELECT e.event_id, e.status, AVG(b.remaining) AS avg_remaining, AVG((b.spent - b.amount) * 1.0 / NULLIF(b.amount, 0)) AS avg_overspend FROM budget b JOIN event e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event GROUP BY e.event_id, e.status), st AS (SELECT status, AVG(avg_remaining) AS avg_remaining, AVG(avg_overspend) AS avg_overspend_rate FROM ev GROUP BY status) SELECT status, avg_remaining, avg_overspend_rate, avg_remaining / AVG(avg_remaining) OVER () AS remaining_ratio FROM st

assumptions.assumption: Status means event.status (from the matched event), not budget.event_status.
Budget lines with amount = 0 give an undefined overspend rate (NULL), so they are ignored in that average rather than causing an error.

The ratio's denominator is the simple mean of the per-status average remaining values (each status weighted equally), computed as a window average over the status rows. Statuses whose average remaining is NULL are ignored.
